value.rationale: A fixed number of innovators is mathematically and empirically distinct from a fixed positive adoption density: the theorem settles their large-population consensus probability, its supercritical survival law and an all-N quantitative comparison. Even full media pressure leaves one rare innovator a strictly positive failure chance 1/q. This is a natural singular-limit question for social contagion, not merely a finite numerical re-evaluation.
